lever: titlegrep: one sentence at the end of step 1 (Locate) of prompts/system.md: if the issue names no identifier or error text, first git grep -n -i -E the title's main terms joined two at a time, in any order, with an optional underscore (an abstract Alpha/beta/gamma example of the pattern), over the *.py files; a hit names the code the title is about.
why: Mechanism (UNDERSPECIFIED_ISSUE -> WRONG_LOCATION): the issue is three words and a link the sandbox cannot open. The word 'table' pulled p4 (200 s, 31 Table experiments), p4_b1024 (15 calls through table.py, pretty.py, repr.py, syntax.py, console.py; markdown.py first at call 16, 81 s; its first edit came as call 41 and got BudgetExceeded) and p4_v0t2 (a 181 s turn rewriting rich/table.py) away from the gold module. Measured on the base snapshot: the line's one search returns exactly one file, rich/markdown.py, the gold file; over the 40 title-only public tasks with two or more terms it hits in 9, gold first in 6 and in the top 3 in 8 (scripts/forty_two/rich_solve/ev_titlegrep.py; docs/forty_two/evidence/rich_solve_titlegrep.txt). Applies outside the 42: fastapi_5624, rich_2943 and rich_3506 (gold ranked first there too).
expected: low-to-maybe: the line fixes the location for 3 of 6 runs; the v7 family was at the right file by 9 s and still failed on semantics (wrong function, a no-op change at the gold hunk, or 3 broken table tests). The fix must stop the cell style from being painted over already-highlighted inline code (1 of 12 L4 runs did, at 231 s)
alternative: submissions/v13_redfirst (fastapi agent, 02d63d094e85ff0f4ea44c5c247857a938ed766f) for the semantic half: a red-first check that renders inline code inside and outside a table cell would show the lost colours; it does nothing for location. rich-b's submissions/v13_title_repro (origin/forty-two-rich-b, bc9d69ef) targets the same title-only class by running user code first; for this title it risks the same Table misreading.
baseline: p4 (v5h2), p4_v7, p4_v7c, p4_v7d, p4_b1024 (v12-b1024), p4_v0t2 (v0-think) all failed; 1 of 12 Kaggle L4 runs solved (g4-l4-v12)
regression_risk: Fires on every title-only issue: 45 of the 74 public tasks by the test in reach.py (31 in the 42). On the 31 of 40 measured ones where it hits nothing it costs one search call (about 2-5 s). On a hit list without the gold file (rich_3043: console.py instead of _export_format.py) it can pull the first read to a neighbour; step 1's 'usually in the top few hits' still applies. Inferred, not measured on a model.
scoring_risk: Gold fails this task's hidden test under Pygments 2.21.0 and passes under 2.20.0 (the Kaggle pin; measured in the write-up). The box sandbox's Pygments version is not recorded anywhere in this repository, so a correct patch might read as failed on the box; check the box venv's Pygments before reading a 0 of 3.
box_risk: Text-call leaks are not new (10 leaked replies over the six earlier box runs, all recovered after the nudge); new on the v13 screen is one first-reply leak that never recovered (fastapi_14487), cause undecided, v13 not treated as broken. This bundle inherits v13's fenced heredoc in step 3; the added sentence has no fenced block, backtick, brace or tool-call-shaped text (pinned by tests/test_v13_rich_solve.py). A sample with 0 tool calls points at the base, not at this lever.
